lines.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. This is your captain speaking.
We'll be making six stops this week. I'm afraid none of them are on time.
Please keep your seatbelts fastened.
On your left, the Strait of Hormuz.
Closed in February. Reopened in April. Closed again.
It remains closed.
In October, a ship was struck there nearly every day.
Diesel is six dollars twenty-eight a gallon. Please plan your onward travel accordingly.
Coming up on the right, Juneau, Alaska.
The Justice Department is suing to stop Alaska certifying its Senate race, unless Senator Dan Sullivan wins.
The reason given: possible confusion with a second candidate named Sullivan.
On who ordered it, the President said: I'm the one that said do it.
The matter is now in court. Election day is November the third.
Below us, Israel, which voted on Tuesday.
Forming a government takes sixty-one of a hundred and twenty seats.
One exit poll gave Netanyahu's bloc fifty-two. Two others, a tie.
Passengers should expect delays.
We are now crossing Brazil.
Lula has won a fourth term, with just over fifty-one percent.
He won at eighty. Two days later, he turned eighty-one.
The runner-up has lodged a complaint.
Approaching Belgrade.
A student-led list has won the parliamentary election. About two point two million votes to one point seven, by the President's own count.
His words: it is clear that we have lost these elections.
Ladies and gentlemen, the ruling party has conceded.
And finally, Caracas.
Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado is back, after about ten months abroad.
Welcome home. Her next request: an election date.
A quick recap before we land.
One strait, closed. One lawsuit, in court. One count, delayed. One result, disputed. One election, conceded. One leader, home.
Our next departure is scheduled for November the third.
Thank you for flying with us, and for your patience.
